notes:
Account summary: Latency Bridge Digital (mid-market analytics SaaS). Building an agentic in-app assistant for customer ops — triage, run queries, create tickets, and trigger actions in 3rd-party tools. Primary goal: low-latency interactive agent (streaming first bytes) and deterministic tool-call behavior (search -> action flows).

Workload summary: chat-first agentic workflows with multi-step tool use (search index, DB query, ticketing API). Expected baseline: 120-200 concurrent user sessions during peak; average session 10-15 turns; ~80 tokens/turn. Latency SLOs: first-byte streaming <= 250ms typical, tool-call end-to-end (including plugin/http call) <= 1s median, <5% tail >2s. Throughput: spikes up to 600 qps for short windows. Cost sensitivity moderate — will trade to meet SLOs but want predictable unit economics.

Model preferences: open to Llama2/Redwood-verified variants with quantization for cost. Want ability to pin model versions and route to cheaper variants for non-critical queries. Ask: graceful fallback to smaller model for large bursts; auto-fallback to Dedicated pools if hosted capacity constrained.

Security/compliance: SSO/SAML required for admin console. Need audit logging for agent actions and tool calls (independent logs). EU data residency for enterprise customers; KMS support. Legal has flagged retention and export controls.

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2024-09-18: Intro discovery call (Maya) — product overview, attach use-case doc.
- 2024-09-26: Demo of Hosted API streaming + function calls (ff_2024-10-12_latbridge_demo_47a2). AE: Maya, SE: Ravi.
- 2024-10-03: Security deep-dive w/ security team; asked for SOC2 + architecture diagram. Drive: security-faq.docx submitted.
- 2024-10-18: POC kickoff on Hosted API (integration with search and ticketing tool). Initial integration showed tool-call failures under synthetic burst.
- 2024-10-24: SE run synthetic load test (100, 300, 600 qps windows). Observed ~12-15% tool-call timeouts at peak; session stalls. Jira: SRE-217 opened.
- 2024-11-01: Price/packaging sync — Latency Bridge requested Dedicated sizing estimate for 200 concurrent agents and burst buffers.
- 2024-11-07: Follow-up call — confirmed need for idempotent retries and observability for each tool call.

Notes from calls / quotes: 
- Head of Product (A. Morales): "Tool calls are our biggest reliability risk — when a ticket API times out, the agent gives incorrect feedback or gets stuck."
- SE notes (Ravi): "We need fine-grained traces per function-call, plus baked-in retry/backoff and a clear story for duplicate action prevention. Also want streaming partial-results while waiting for long tool calls."
- AE (Maya): "POC must show streaming + consistent tool-call behavior under 3x expected peak. If hosted passes, customer wants Dedicated pricing for reserved capacity."

POC specifics and acceptance criteria: 
- Implement Hosted API integration with streaming responses + function/tool-calls.
- Run synthetic load: 3x expected peak (600 qps) for 10-minute windows; tool-call success rate >= 98%.
- Measure first-byte latencies and p95/p99 for streaming chunks.
- Demonstrate retry semantics and idempotency for ticket creation actions; show audit log entries per action.
- Provide cost estimate for Dedicated pool to meet 200 concurrent agents + 2x burst capacity.

Open action items / next steps: 
- SE (Ravi) to provide Dedicated sizing worksheet and failed-call mitigation patterns (by 2024-11-12).
- Engineering to share tracing hooks and sampling configuration for function calls (attach example logs).
- Customer to run second POC run with revised retry/backoff and report results.
- Legal to start procurement review once SOC2 artifacts provided.

- Tool-call timeouts under burst not yet solved.
- Pricing model clarity: concurrent agent vs token billing trade-offs.
